PASS with caveats. (1) This is a behaviour-coded infant/child imitation task, not a questionnaire: item_text holds the three demonstrated target actions as Vaporova & Zmyj (2020) name them in their Coding section, and option_text holds the S1 Data header's own value labels (0 = not imitated, 1 = imitated). No wording was read to participants for the items themselves, so item_text is a literal transcript of the source's action labels rather than of anything a respondent saw. (2) instructions holds the single utterance the experimenter did make - "Now you may play with the mouse!" - which was administered in German at TU Dortmund; the paper prints only its English, and neither the S1 Data workbook nor the PLOS supporting information (S1 Data, S1-S3 Video) carries the German original, so language=German with English in the base fields and empty _translated columns (text_source=translated_substitute, translation_source=study_supplied). (3) Rights: no restriction locatable on the wording. The paper is CC BY 4.0; the task is Barr/Hayne-style three-step deferred-imitation procedure, not a commercially published instrument, and there is no rights holder page stating a fee, a non-commercial or a no-redistribution term. No row in instrument_rights_register.csv matches. Silence is permission (irw#1945).
